Video 12 - harness engineering
Okay, so if you have been anywhere near Twitter, or whatever we are calling X now, over the last few
months, you have probably seen this everywhere - Harness Engineering. And your first reaction was
probably the same as mine. Is this a new job title in AI? Do I need to learn this too? Is this just
another fancy name for prompt engineering? The short answer is, No. It is not another name for
writing better prompts. It is actually describing something very real and important today. And by the
end of this video, we will understand exactly what harness engineering is, why it suddenly matters so
much, and how you can become a harness engineer as well. So, let’s get into it. Imagine someone gives you the most powerful car engine money can buy.

brakes, in fact it does not even have a seat for you to sit on. This engine you have, does not even
know it is supposed to be inside the car. Its job is really small.

orchestration, context engineering, prompt engineering and what not. Harness engineering is simply

an umbrella term that brings all of those ideas together. So that is not new. The reason everyone is
suddenly talking about it is because the bottleneck has changed. For years, most of the improvement
in AI came from better models. Every new generation of models companies have been launching,
have been way smarter than the previous one. But today, the frontier models are already very
capable. Simply switching from one top tier model to another, does not transform the product as it
used to. Today, two teams can start with the exact same model and still end up with completely
different quality of products. The difference is not the model anymore, it is harness.

So let us get concrete. What are we actually talking about when we say the harness? Here are the
few big pieces. First one is context management. This is about two questions actually. First, what is
context? And second, why does managing it matter? See, the context window is, everything your
model can see while answering your question. That includes the question you asked, your
conversation history, the system prompt, tool outputs, uploaded documents - basically everything
the model is processing at that moment. You see this news from google introducing the 2-million
context window model? They keep making models with larger and larger context windows. But no
matter how large the context window is, it is still finite.

ntext window model? They keep making models with larger and larger context windows. But no
matter how large the context window is, it is still finite. Which means you have to decide what
deserves to be inside that context window. Your harness should make sure the model only receives
the documents, tool outputs, and information that actually matters for answering current question. The second is, Tools. As we saw earlier, the model only works with text. It does not browse the web. It does not execute code. It does not make phone calls. To make it useful, we have to connect it to
external tools. Let’s take one example here, web search.

what has to be searched online, which API should be called and with what parameters, and writes
the code for that API request. But it cannot actually send that request. A search tool like Tavily or
SerpAPI does that part. So the model is writing the request, the tool is executing it. Together, they
become a complete pipeline. The better you design and orchestrate these tools, the better your
harness becomes. The third is Feedback loops. Let’s understand it using the same example. Suppose the model did

maximum number of attempts, or minimum quality score or a timeout, to let the model know when
to stop trying. Without these guardrails, you will end up with infinite loops, runaway costs, and all
kinds of unexpected behaviour. The next is Memory and state. AI systems do not finish tasks in one step.Tasks involve planning,
reasoning, calling multiple tools, and revisiting previous decisions. The system will need memory for

is why, harness engineering is becoming the real competitive advantage today, because it is indeed
the most important skill in AI. The last is, how to actually think like a harness engineer? You need to start asking questions like,
what information does the model actually need at each step? What all can go wrong in each step and
how do we make sure to catch it in time? What should happen if the model gets stuck in any step? At
what point, should a human step in? We are not writing one clever prompt anymore. We are thinking

CONSULTANCY AGREEMENT FOR AI, DATA ANALYTICS AND
RELATED SERVICES
AGREEMENT DATE
August 13th 2026

PARTIES
COMPANY: Nexora Intelligence Private Limited, a company incorporated in India, having its corporate
office at 5th Floor, Meridian Tech Park, Madhapur, Hyderabad, Telangana 500081.
CONSULTANT: Rhea Anaya, Resident of Banjara Hills, Hyderabad, Telangana 500034.

BACKGROUND
The Company is engaged in artificial intelligence, software development, data analytics, machine learning,
and related consulting services.
The Consultant has technical knowledge, skill, and experience relevant to artificial intelligence, data
analytics, and related technology services.
The Company has requested the Consultant to provide consultancy services, and the Consultant has
agreed to provide those services.

APPOINTMENT AND ROLE
The Company appoints the Consultant to provide consultancy services in artificial intelligence, data
analytics, and related technology services.
CONSULTANT ROLE: AI Solutions Consultant

SCOPE OF SERVICES
1. Design, develop, test, and support artificial intelligence and machine learning solutions.
2. Prepare, transform, validate, and analyze data required for AI and analytics initiatives.
3. Assist with retrieval-augmented generation systems, including document processing, retrieval,
evaluation, and related AI workflows.
4. Assist with intelligent automation and other generative AI applications.
5. Conduct experimentation, benchmarking, model evaluation, and trend analysis.
6. Interpret analytical and model outputs and communicate findings through reports, dashboards, and
presentations.
7. Participate in AI and data projects with the Company and its clients.
8. Provide other related consultancy services reasonably requested by the Company.

FEES AND COMPENSATION
FIXED FEE: Rs. 1,85,000 per Month. The Consultant will invoice the Company on the first day of each
month for services provided and performed.
VARIABLE FEE: None. The Consultant is entitled only to the fixed monthly fee described above, unless the
parties later agree otherwise in writing.
ADDITIONAL COMPENSATION: None.
INVOICE PAYMENT: The Company will pay valid invoices within 5 working days after receipt.

TAXES: TDS and other applicable deductions will be handled according to applicable law.
PAYMENT METHOD: Payments will be made by bank transfer to the bank account designated by the
Consultant.

EXPENSES
The Consultant may claim reimbursement for reasonable and necessary expenses incurred while providing
services. All such expenses must be approved by the Company in writing before they are incurred, and the
Consultant must provide receipts or other proof of payment.

TERM
EFFECTIVE DATE: September 1st 2026
EXPIRY DATE: August 31st 2027
The Agreement automatically renews for one-year periods unless either party terminates it in writing with
one month's notice.
The Company may terminate the Agreement immediately in the event of a material breach by the
Consultant.
INDEPENDENT CONTRACTOR
The Consultant is an independent contractor and not an employee of the Company. This Agreement does
not create a partnership, joint venture, or agency relationship between the parties.

EXCLUSIVITY
During the term of this Agreement, the Consultant will not enter into a competing engagement that
materially conflicts with the Consultant's obligations under this Agreement without the Company's prior
written consent.

OWNERSHIP OF WORK PRODUCT
All work product created by the Consultant specifically for the Company or its clients while performing the
services will remain the exclusive property of the Company or the applicable client, subject to any separate
written agreement.

CONFIDENTIALITY
The Consultant must keep confidential all non-public information, materials, data, documentation, business
information, technical information, and terms of this Agreement received or created during the engagement.
The Consultant may not disclose or use confidential information outside the scope of this Agreement
without prior written consent, except when disclosure is required by law.

GOVERNING LAW
This Agreement will be governed by the laws of India. The courts of Hyderabad, Telangana will have
jurisdiction.

SEVERABILITY
If any provision of this Agreement is found to be invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions will
continue in effect.

AMENDMENTS
Any amendment to this Agreement must be made in writing and signed by both parties.

RETURN OF COMPANY PROPERTY
Upon termination of this Agreement, the Consultant must return Company property, equipment, documents,
and confidential materials in the Consultant's possession.
